situation.name: wormhole-chain-baton
situation.description: A substrate is seeded with a single hand-placed signal cell in Attract state and a serpentine chain of Abstain relay cells whose d values encode the next hop (cell with d=k must route to the cell whose d=k+1) across a 64-slot wormhole table. The task is to hand the packet from hop 0 to hop 63 within a fixed tick budget, but several chain cells share the same d (forced 64-slot collisions), so LAST-WRITER-WINS (M4) makes the chain non-deterministic in hop order unless authors avoid collisions. A second adversarial arm places the chain with two consecutive relays at identical d, guaranteeing a collision, and the metric is how many hops complete before the packet stalls or loops.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Place Attract cells at a sparse deterministic grid: every cell (x,y) with (x mod 13 == 0 and y mod 7 == 0) is Attract. Repel cells at (x mod 17 == 3 and y mod 11 == 5). Abstain relay chain: start at (4,4), then for k=0..63 place an Abstain cell at (4 + ((k*7) mod 88), 4 + ((k*3) mod 56)), setting its d := k. Ground elsewhere. In arm B (collision), override the d of hop 33 to equal hop 32's d (both 32), then continue numbering hops 34.. from d=33 as before, so exactly one duplicate d exists and one d value is skipped.
substrate_spec.task: Starting from the cell whose d=0, the packet must be handed via wormhole slot reads (M4) hop-by-hop: at each tick, the current Abstain cell reads slot d, and if that slot is occupied by a different cell with nonzero resonance, the next hop becomes that cell; the packet must reach the cell whose d=63 within a pre-registered tick budget, with no hop visited twice.
substrate_spec.metric: Number of distinct hops completed before either reaching d=63, stalling (no different-cell slot read for 3 consecutive ticks), or revisiting a hop; and total ticks consumed. Measured from the sealed trace hash.
substrate_spec.floor: PRE-REGISTERED: in arm A (collision-free chain) the packet reaches d=63 in <= 64 ticks with zero revisits and zero stalls. In arm B (one duplicated d) the packet must fail by stalling or revisiting within 64 ticks; a run that reaches d=63 in arm B is a falsification of the collision-loss claim. Band: arm A completion rate >= 0.99 over 100 seeds; arm B completion rate <= 0.01.
substrate_spec.why_interesting: Prices M4's last-writer-wins slot-collision rule as a routing hazard, and C2 (wormhole beats graph-traversal) by forcing non-local alignment through a 64-slot table with contention; it also stresses A1/A2 bounds invariance under chained d reassignment.

situation.name: abstain-slot-contention-storm
situation.description: A 64x64 substrate is seeded so that 512 Abstain cells are funneled by a deterministic drift field onto only 8 distinct data values d in {7,15,23,31,39,47,55,63}, while 256 Attract cells and 256 Repel cells are placed to keep real-channel accumulators oscillating around zero so that |real_acc| stays small and resonance = |real_acc|+1 stays near 1. At each tick every Abstain cell tries to WRITE its (x,y) and resonance into slot d (M4); because many cells share the same d, slot collisions are resolved last-writer-wins, so twin resonance for readers of a slot usually fires against whatever cell wrote last, not against a spatially or semantically aligned twin. The task is to measure how much twin-resonance signal is lost relative to a control substrate where the same number of Abstain cells are spread across 64 distinct d values.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Deterministic: (1) Ground = all cells where (x+y) mod 5 == 0. (2) Attract = cells where (x*3+y*7) mod 17 < 4 and not Ground. (3) Repel = cells where (x*5+y*11) mod 19 < 4 and not Ground and not Attract. (4) Abstain = remaining cells whose initial d is forced to one of the 8 contested values by d = 7 + 8*((x*13+y*29) mod 8), so each contested slot receives approximately 64 writers. (5) No two cells share (x,y); placement is a pure function of coordinates and seed, no runtime discovery.

situation.task: Run 64 ticks; at each tick count the number of Abstain read events (slot reads triggered by an Abstain cell carrying d) and, among those, the number that fire twin resonance against a DIFFERENT cell with nonzero resonance (M4). Compare against a control run with identical geometry but d spread uniformly over 0..63 (one cell per slot). The substrate must report per-tick resonance-hit ratio and the number of distinct writers per slot.
situation.metric: Contention-starvation ratio R = (resonance-hit count in contested run) / (resonance-hit count in uniform-d control), both at tick 64, with the same total Abstain cell count and same geometry. Secondary: mean distinct writers per slot and slot churn rate (last-writer switches per tick per slot).
situation.floor: Falsifiable prediction: at tick 64, R <= 0.35, i.e. the contested substrate delivers at most 35% of the control's twin-resonance hits, and mean distinct writers per slot >= 32. If R > 0.35 the contention-starvation claim is falsified and the M4 last-writer-wins mechanism is exonerated for this geometry.
situation.why_interesting: Prices C2 (wormhole beats graph-traversal for non-local alignment) under adversarial load: it tests whether the 64-slot wormhole table is a genuine non-local alignment mechanism or a collision-prone bus whose usefulness collapses when Abstain cells crowd a few d values. It also stress-tests M4's last-writer-wins as a hidden pathology: the slot table may be a compile-time blueprint (M4) but its runtime contention policy is an unpriced assumption, and this scenario measures whether that assumption starves twin resonance.

situation.name: armor-ring-portal-pincer
situation.description: A closed Moore-8 ring of Attract cells (tau=1) is the armor; at every 8th ring position sits an Abstain cell (tau=3) whose data value equals its ring index, declaring a 64-slot wormhole endpoint (M4). An adversary cannot write directly into ring cells, so every strike must enter THROUGH a portal: each tick it picks a portal, reads slot d (the twin-resonance read side of M4), and injects a Repel cell (tau=2) into the ring's void interior adjacent to the portal's twin, simultaneously flipping the struck ring cell's tau from Attract to Repel. The ring must re-seal: Attract pressure (M5) must push damaged d-values back toward saturation, and the portal's imaginary-channel handshake (M4) must re-fire when the ring's own resonance exceeds the injected |real_acc|+1.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Ring = all cells (x,y) with Chebyshev distance 30 from center (32,32), every one tau=1 (Attract) with d = min(63, 8 + (arctan2(y-32,x-32) mod 8)); the 8 portal cells are those ring positions where ring-index mod 8 == 0, tau=3 (Abstain), d = ring-index (0..56 step 8), resonance written into wormhole slot d each tick (M4 write side). Interior and exterior all tau=0 (Ground), d=0. Adversary is a deterministic scripted process, not part of the vector pass.

situation.task: Maintain a fully Attract, saturation-pushed ring (all ring cells tau=1, all d=63) for 200 ticks despite adversarial portal injections every tick; a tick is 'healed' when every struck cell has tau=1 and d>=60, and the portal's slot-d read returns a twin with resonance > injected |real_acc|+1.
situation.metric: Ticks-to-reseal (max over all strikes of ticks from injection until healed) and total healed-strikes / total-strikes over 200 ticks; both read from the sealed trace, integer-only (A3, M6).
situation.floor: Pre-registered: median ticks-to-reseal <= 12 AND healed-strikes/total-strikes >= 0.90 for attacks whose injected |real_acc| <= 8; if either fails by the letter it is labeled post-hoc, never rewritten (house law). Wormhole OFF arm must reseal >= 25% slower or fail C2.
situation.why_interesting: Prices C5 (self-repair band) and C2 (wormhole vs no-wormhole traversal) inside the same substrate, with C3 adjacent: run the sigma sweep {log2(3),0.5,1,2,4} on portal bridge stability and C4's theta>pi/4 threshold on the imaginary-channel handshake — all four claims get paired arms from one byte-identical seed (M6).

selection_reasons: CR1: floor must be quantitative and falsifiable from the trace alone (pre-registerable without re-reading the prose). CR2: must price an OPEN claim (C2/C4/C5) or a review finding (R1/R3) — no situation that only decorates. CR3: must run on the reference kernel AS SPECDED (wormhole table + Moore-8 + timbre table) with no new primitives.

situation.name: knife-edge-checkerboard-cascade
situation.description: A 128x64 substrate is tiled in a strict checkerboard of Attract (tau=1) and Repel (tau=2) cells, with a thin Ground (tau=0) seam down the central column and a handful of Abstain (tau=3) cells planted on the seam. At tick 0 exactly one border cell on the seam has its byte flipped from Attract to Repel. The substrate must decide, within a bounded tick window, whether the flip is absorbed locally or propagates across the whole board via Moore-8 real-accumulator pressure (M5) and wormhole bridges (M4). Theta (C4) is swept across the knife edge where the two outcomes trade dominance.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: tau = 1 if (x+y) mod 2 == 0 else 2, for all cells with x != 63; central column x=63 forced to tau=0 (Ground seam); at (63, y) for y in {8, 24, 40, 56} place tau=3 (Abstain) with d = 32; all d initialised to 32 except the flipped cell at (64, 32) which is set to tau=2, d=32 at tick 0.

situation.task: Detect whether the single flipped byte produces a substrate-wide phase inversion (>=90% of originally-Attract cells flipping sign of their real accumulator by tick T=256) or dies within a radius r<=4 of the flip site. The substrate must be run twice: wormhole ON (M4 active) and wormhole OFF (tau=3 cells treated as Ground), with theta swept over {0, pi/8, pi/4, 3pi/8, pi/2}.
situation.metric: For each (wormhole_state, theta) arm: ticks-to-global-inversion, final inversion fraction, and the radius of the dead-flip case at tick 256. Trace hash sealed per arm (M6).
situation.floor: Pre-registered: wormhole ON at theta=pi/4 must reach >=90% inversion in <=128 ticks in at least 4 of 5 seeds; wormhole OFF must fail to reach >=50% inversion in >=4 of 5 seeds. If both arms land in the same regime at theta=pi/4, C4's claimed threshold is falsified for this substrate.
situation.why_interesting: Directly prices C4 (phase threshold theta > pi/4 triggers useful non-local transfer) and C2 (wormhole beats local traversal) on the same substrate, with a single-byte perturbation as the only input, so any cascade is unambiguously attributable to the threshold and the wormhole, not to initial energy.

selection_reasons: CR1: floor must be quantitative and falsifiable from the trace alone (pre-registerable without re-reading the prose). CR2: must price an OPEN claim (C2/C4/C5) or a review finding (R1/R3) — no situation that only decorates. CR3: must run on the reference kernel AS SPECDED (wormhole table + Moore-8 + timbre table) with no new primitives.

situation.name: moore-handed-race-c2
situation.description: A 32x32 substrate is cut into two disconnected Moore-8 components by a 2-cell-wide Ground moat; component L holds a planted source pattern and component R holds its unique twin pattern, spatially offset so no local propagation path exists. Arm ON uses tau=3 Abstain cells on both sides whose d codes are the twin keys, so M4 twin-resonance can bridge the moat in a single tick; arm OFF replaces all tau=3 cells with tau=1 Attract cells, handing Moore-8 diffusion every possible advantage: same total cell count, same d values, maximal local pressure, zero abstention tax. The metric is ticks-to-first-cross-component alignment event under a fixed 400-tick cap; if the wormhole cannot beat diffusion on a task that was deliberately constructed so diffusion must walk, C2 is dead.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Deterministic: columns 15-16 all rows are tau=0 Ground (moat, d=0). Component L = columns 0-14, component R = columns 17-31. In component L, cells where (x+y) mod 8 == 0 are tau=1 Attract with d=((x*7+y*13) mod 48)+8; cells where (x+y) mod 8 == 4 are tau=2 Repel with d=((x*11+y*5) mod 32)+1; remaining L cells tau=0 Ground d=0. Mirror the same rule in R with x' = x-17, but XOR the low 3 bits of every nonzero d with 0b101 so L and R patterns are non-trivially paired, not translations. Arm ON only: additionally place tau=3 Abstain cells at a fixed list of 12 positions in L (rows 4,10,16,22,28 at cols 2,7,12) and the same 12 rows at cols 19,24,29 in R; the d of each L abstain cell equals the d of its designated R twin after the XOR, so slot d in the M4 wormhole table is keyed identically on both sides. Arm OFF only: those same 24 positions are tau=1 Attract with d equal to the abstain cell's d; everything else byte-identical. Both arms share seed, size, moat, attract/repel skeleton, and total cell count.

situation.task: Within 400 ticks, produce a first cross-component alignment event: an M4 twin-resonance fire in which an Abstain cell in L reads a wormhole slot last written by an Abstain cell in R (or vice versa) with nonzero resonance, OR in arm OFF the analogous event defined as a Repel/Attract phase-lock where the real accumulator of a cell in R first matches the XOR-key of a cell in L to within +-1. The event must be detected from the trace alone; no oracle knowledge of planted pairs is allowed at runtime.
situation.metric: ticks-to-first-cross-component-alignment-event; secondary: total bytes-touched (sum of nonzero d reads/writes per tick) and fired-twin count. Trace hash sealed per tick for determinism (M6).
situation.floor: Pre-registered falsifier for C2: arm ON must achieve first alignment in <= 40 ticks AND strictly fewer ticks than arm OFF by at least a factor of 2 (ON < OFF/2) in at least 3 of 3 independent seeds {1337, 4242, 9001}. If arm OFF reaches alignment first in any seed, or if ON exceeds 40 ticks in any seed, C2 is falsified for this task and the wormhole does not earn its keep against Moore-8 diffusion. Secondary pre-registration: bytes-touched for ON must not exceed OFF by more than 20% before the alignment tick, so the win cannot be bought by brute-force scanning.

situation.name: channel-shear-r2-crossing
situation.description: A 64x64 substrate is laid out as two interleaved combs: even rows are a real-channel transport lane (Attract/Repel only, no Abstain), odd rows are an imaginary-channel lane (Abstain only on a fixed diagonal, Ground elsewhere). At tick 0 the real lance is driven left-to-right and the imaginary lance top-to-bottom, so every real cell eventually sits adjacent (Moore-8, M5) to an Abstain cell whose wormhole slot d (M4) was written by a cell on the other axis. The shear is: the real lane's M5 accumulation is updated in the SAME tick as the imaginary lane's M4 slot reads/writes, with no barrier between them. We measure whether the composed trace is identical to the trace produced by running the two lanes sequentially with a barrier (R2 commutation made physical: do the real update and the imaginary wormhole update commute under same-tick interleaving?).

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Row parity fixes lane. If (y mod 2)==0: cells with x in {1,4,7,...,61} (x mod 3 == 1) are Attract (tau=1, d = (x*7 + y) mod 64); cells with x mod 3 == 2 are Repel (tau=2, d = (x*5 + y*3) mod 64); all other even-row cells are Ground. If (y mod 2)==1: cells with (x+y) mod 8 == 0 lie on the imaginary diagonal and are Abstain (tau=3, d = (x + y) mod 64); all other odd-row cells are Ground. No cell is both lanes; the only cross-lane coupling is M5 Moore-8 adjacency between an even row and its odd-row neighbors.

situation.task: Run N=200 ticks of the full same-tick interleaved update (real M5 and imaginary M4 fired inside one tick over a snapshot read) and record the full 4096-byte trace per tick. Then run the barrier variant: each tick computes all M5 real updates against the previous tick, commits, THEN computes all M4 wormhole reads/writes against that committed state, and record its trace. The substrate must produce both traces under the same seed and same initial placement.
situation.metric: Per-tick Hamming distance between the interleaved trace and the barrier trace, summed over 200 ticks and normalized by 4096*200 (fraction of bits that differ); PLUS count of ticks where a wormhole slot d collides between two Abstain cells (M4 last-writer-wins) in the interleaved run but not the barrier run.
situation.floor: Pre-registered prediction: the interleaved and barrier traces are byte-identical for all 200 ticks (normalized Hamming = 0.0000, collision-count difference = 0). Falsified if normalized Hamming > 0 on any tick OR if collision-count difference > 0. A secondary band: if not identical, the first divergence appears no later than tick 3 (the first tick at which a real lane cell is Moore-adjacent to an Abstain cell), stated as tick_of_first_divergence <= 3.
situation.why_interesting: Prices the R2 commutation question against M4/M5/M6: if the interleaved and barrier traces are byte-identical, the real and imaginary channels commute under same-tick composition and the wormhole table is a genuinely separable compile-time layer (consistent with M4's 'zero runtime discovery' claim). If they diverge, M6 determinism still holds for each arm but the composition order is a hidden degree of freedom the spec never pinned, which would make C1's 'intra-cell timbre vs inter-cell porting' comparison ill-defined unless composition order is pre-registered. It also probes whether M4's last-writer-wins collision rule is stable under real-channel pressure that shifts which Abstain cells carry nonzero |real_acc|+1 resonance into slots.

situation.name: slot-collision-cooker
situation.description: A 64x1 substrate where every column is an Abstain cell, so all 64 cells share the SAME data value d=0 and therefore contend for exactly one wormhole-table slot per tick. Each tick every cell writes its own (x,y) and resonance=|real_acc|+1 into slot 0; last-writer-wins means the rightmost writer survives while 63 twin-resonance events are culled. Over 64 ticks we count how many distinct cells ever fire twin resonance versus the 64x64=4096 write attempts, exposing the culling rate as a function of contention.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: All cells tau=3 (Abstain), d=0. Tie-break for last-writer-wins is column index order left-to-right, so cell x=63 always wins slot 0 on any tick it writes. Resonance seeds are distinct per cell: resonance(x)=x+1 at placement, so a surviving read from cell x into cell x' yields imaginary += resonance(x')*log2(3) only when x' is the current occupant.

situation.task: Over exactly 64 ticks, record for each tick which cell occupied slot 0 (the writer) and which cell read a DIFFERENT nonzero-resonance occupant (the twin-resonance firer). Accumulate: total twin-resonance firings, distinct cells that ever fired, and the imaginary-channel magnitude summed across ticks.
situation.metric: Twin-resonance survival rate = (total twin-resonance firings) / (total write attempts = 64 cells x 64 ticks = 4096), plus count of distinct cells that ever fired (0..64).
situation.floor: Pre-registered falsifiable prediction: with 64-way contention and left-to-right last-writer-wins, distinct cells that ever fire twin resonance is exactly 0 (the writer never reads a DIFFERENT occupant, since it overwrites then reads its own cell), so survival rate <= 0.0156 (1/64). If any distinct-cell firing is observed, M4's last-writer-wins is misimplemented.
situation.why_interesting: Prices M4's last-writer-wins under maximal slot pressure and gives R3 (the collision pathology) a physical trace: it separates 'the wormhole table works' from 'the wormhole table works only when contention is low.' If the predicted 0 distinct firers holds, M4 is confirmed as a strictly local-occupancy mechanism, which sharpens the C2 wormhole-vs-graph comparison by bounding the non-local bandwidth to one live slot per d.

selection_reasons: CR1: floor must be quantitative and falsifiable from the trace alone (pre-registerable without re-reading the prose). CR2: must price an OPEN claim (C2/C4/C5) or a review finding (R1/R3) — no situation that only decorates. CR3: must run on the reference kernel AS SPECDED (wormhole table + Moore-8 + timbre table) with no new primitives.

situation.name: saturation-front-twin-at-the-rails
situation.description: A 48x48 substrate is pinned so that a vertical wall of Attract cells at d=63 faces a vertical wall of Repel cells at d=0, separated by one column of Abstain cells carrying distinct d values. The update rule (M5) drives the left wall toward saturation min(d+1,63) and the right wall toward 0, so the interface column is the only place where nonzero real_acc can still change sign. The question is whether the wormhole table (M4) routes any signal across the pinned front when local pressure is constant and the real channel is effectively dead.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Column x=0: tau=1 (Attract), d=63. Columns x=1..22: tau=0 (Ground), d=0. Column x=23: tau=3 (Abstain), d = (y mod 64), one Abstain cell per row, resonance initialized to 0. Columns x=24..46: tau=0 (Ground), d=0. Column x=47: tau=2 (Repel), d=0. No other cells. Deterministic, no randomness.

situation.task: Run 200 ticks. At each tick, each Abstain cell at x=23 reads slot d and writes (x,y,resonance=|real_acc|+1) last-writer-wins. Measure the number of distinct twin-resonance firings (slot read hit by a different cell with nonzero resonance) and the number of distinct (y1,y2) row pairs that ever bridge. Then re-run with the wormhole table disabled (Abstain treated as Ground) as the control arm.
situation.metric: Count of distinct row-pairs (y1,y2) that ever produce a twin-resonance firing, plus the first-tick index at which any firing occurs, under wormhole ON vs OFF.
situation.floor: Prediction: with wormhole ON, at least 1 distinct row-pair bridges by tick 40, and the count is strictly greater than the OFF arm by tick 200. Falsified if ON == OFF at every tick, or if no firing occurs by tick 200.
situation.why_interesting: Directly prices C2 (wormhole beats graph-traversal for non-local alignment) at the extreme of A2's bounds, where M5's local rule cannot move the real channel. Also probes whether sigma (M4) matters when real_acc is pinned, feeding C3's sweep.

situation.name: abstain-echo-chamber-trilemma
situation.description: A 16x4 arena is seeded so a central 2x4 block of cells is forced Abstain every tick (tau=3), each carrying distinct data values d in a bijection onto slots 8..15. Peripheral Attract/Repel cells feed a controlled real accumulator so |real_acc| is held non-trivial, making each Abstain cell write resonance = |real_acc|+1 into its slot d each tick. Because slots are keyed by d and each forced cell holds a unique d, no twin-resonance fires between the forced block itself; instead each tick every forced cell READS its slot and finds it occupied by a DIFFERENT cell only when a peripheral 'prober' cell (Abstain, d matching) is injected on schedule. The forcing holds tau constant while letting the imaginary channel accumulate sum over ticks of resonance*sigma. Three outcomes are separable: (a) phase-oscillator behavior — imaginary accumulator tracks a bounded periodic function of tick, sign-flipping each time a prober collides (last-writer-wins alternating ownership of slot d); (b) saturation — imaginary accumulator monotonically rises then clips to a fixed ceiling; (c) collapse — imaginary accumulator decays to zero after a transient because resonance is overwritten by a zero-real-acc writer.

substrate_spec.timbre_placement_rules: Row 1 (y=1), columns 6..9: forced Abstain (tau=3) every tick, d assigned bijectively as d=8+(x-6). Row 0 (y=0) all columns: Attract (tau=1), d=1+(x mod 8). Row 3 (y=3) all columns: Repel (tau=2), d=1+(x mod 8). Row 2 (y=2), columns 0..15: Ground (tau=0). Prober cell: single cell at (x_p, y=2) injected as Abstain (tau=3) with d equal to the forced cell under test, x_p sweeping left-to-right one column per 4 ticks, then wrapping. All placement is a pure function of (x,y,tick) — no RNG after seeding.

situation.task: Run T=64 ticks. For each forced Abstain cell (x in 6..9), record the imaginary accumulator i_x(t) = sum over ticks s<=t of (resonance_written_into_slot_d at tick s) * sigma, with sigma=log2(3). Classify each i_x(t) trajectory as oscillator (>=4 sign changes of the detrended residual AND bounded |i| with max/min ratio < 3), saturating (monotone non-decreasing for >= 80% of ticks AND final/first > 5), or collapsing (|i(T)| < 0.2 * max_t |i(t)|).
situation.metric: Per-cell classification vector over the 4 forced cells plus the aggregate count of distinct classes observed; secondary metric is the period estimate (in ticks) of any oscillator-class cell via zero-crossing spacing.
situation.floor: Pre-registered prediction: at least 3 of the 4 forced cells classify identically, AND the modal class is NOT saturating. Falsified if the 4 cells split 2-2 or if saturating is the modal class. Secondary floor: any oscillator-class cell must have period in [4,32] ticks.
situation.why_interesting: Directly prices C3 (is sigma=log2(3) the critical bridge scale?) and C4 (does phase threshold theta>pi/4 govern non-local transfer?) by making the imaginary channel's long-run behavior the dependent variable. It also stress-tests M4's last-writer-wins collision rule (A2 bounds invariance under forced Abstain) and M6 determinism, since the classification must reproduce byte-identically on re-run.
